nodes.label: Eliminating Waterfalls
nodes.rationale: Waterfalls are the #1 performance killer. Each sequential await adds full network latency. Eliminating them yields the largest gains.

nodes.label: Bundle Size Optimization
nodes.rationale: Reducing initial bundle size improves Time to Interactive and Largest Contentful Paint.

nodes.label: Server-Side Performance
nodes.rationale: Optimizing server-side rendering and data fetching eliminates server-side waterfalls and reduces response times.

nodes.label: Client-Side Data Fetching
nodes.rationale: Automatic deduplication and efficient data fetching patterns reduce redundant network requests.

nodes.label: Re-render Optimization
nodes.rationale: Reducing unnecessary re-renders minimizes wasted computation and improves UI responsiveness.

nodes.label: Rendering Performance
nodes.rationale: Optimizing the rendering process reduces the work the browser needs to do.

nodes.label: JavaScript Performance
nodes.rationale: Micro-optimizations for hot paths can add up to meaningful improvements.

nodes.label: Advanced Patterns
nodes.rationale: Advanced patterns for specific cases that require careful implementation.

nodes.label: useEffectEvent
nodes.rationale: React hook that creates a stable function reference that always calls the latest version of the handler, preventing effect re-runs while avoiding stale closures.

nodes.label: next/dynamic
nodes.rationale: Next.js utility for lazy-loading components at runtime, splitting bundles and deferring code that isn't needed on initial render.

nodes.label: SWR
nodes.rationale: Data fetching library with built-in request deduplication, caching, and revalidation across component instances.

nodes.label: better-all
nodes.rationale: Library for dependency-based parallelization that automatically starts each task at the earliest possible moment.

nodes.label: Module-Level Cache Pattern
nodes.rationale: Use module-level Maps or variables to cache function results across renders, avoiding redundant computation. Use a Map (not a hook) so it works everywhere: utilities, event handlers, not just React components.
